#+title: Native workspace recipe contract

* Delivery state
The Nix recipe implementation supports the closed version2 workspace request
below. BL/Rust client integration and all execution/qualification belong to the
main thread. These implementation changes alone do not establish a supported
production target or close the final acceptance gates.

* Request and provenance
#+begin_src json
{"version":2,"source":"/nix/store/WORKSPACE-SNAPSHOT",
 "member":"crates/engine","package":"rust-engine","crate":"engine",
 "abi":"beam-lisp-native-engine-v1","target":"x86_64-linux"}
#+end_src

source names the complete explicit workspace closure root. It contains the
root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, selected member, sibling path dependencies and
supporting files. member is the package directory relative to that root;
"." selects a root package. package must equal that manifest's package.name.
crate remains the BL-facing library identity. Cargo's lib.name can differ.

The version2 artifact retains exact source/member/package/crate/abi/target,
records cargoLibrary as the actual Cargo library name, and publishes the stable
lib/<crate>.so path. Toolchain identity, final-byte digest, compiled product and
worker observations remain in the manifest. Version1 request and artifact
fields remain compatible with standalone crates.

* Snapshot and validation
native-source.nix and native-snapshot.nix accept version (default1), member
(default".") and package (default null). Version2 requires package explicitly.
The snapshot omits .git, .bl and target directories and refuses symlinks or
special files. Direct version2 store inputs must already be filtered snapshots.

Validation parses the root, selected member and transitive path dependencies.
It checks ordinary/dev/build/target-specific/workspace dependency tables and
patch/replace declarations. Paths normalize within the captured root; absolute
or escaping paths and reserved build/cache paths refuse. Cargo owns workspace
member-glob expansion and complete locked-workspace consistency. Unused invalid
Cargo.toml test fixtures are retained as support bytes without being parsed.

Workspace-inherited package versions are resolved from workspace.package.
Member paths are bounded ASCII relative segments: no empty/dot/dot-dot,
reserved or leading-hyphen segments; each segment is at most255 characters,
and the whole member is at most4096 characters. Cargo package names and Rust
library/BL crate identifiers are bounded to128 characters. Path normalization
is bounded to4096 characters, source depth to64, and the inspected manifest
closure to1024 entries.

* Build behavior
The fixed recipe passes --lib, --manifest-path <member>/Cargo.toml and --package
<package>. It pins CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target so project Cargo configuration cannot
redirect publication. Cargo.lock is always the root lock. All compilation
remains in the bounded KVM worker; no writable Cargo target is published.

Version2 snapshots have a workspace-wide name, and compiled products use the
Cargo package/library identity. Changing only the BL alias or ABI label changes
the wrapper without changing the Rust compile inputs. The existing desktop
profile follows the selected Cargo/library identity for version2. Additional
system-dependency profiles remain separate declared-recipe work.

* Main-thread qualification cases
- Existing version1 standalone realization and BL/Rust byte agreement.
- Workspace root with inherited version, a differently named cdylib, and a
  sibling path dependency; invoke the resulting native function.
- Root package plus nested path dependency; transitive ../sibling paths that
  normalize inside the root; workspace.dependencies and target/build/dev paths.
- Root Cargo.lock and support-file/build.rs changes affect the product;
  generated target noise does not affect a normal snapshot.
- Alias-only and ABI-only changes reuse compiled while final manifests differ.
- An unused deliberately invalid Cargo.toml fixture does not block the package.
- Absolute/escaping/missing dependency paths, symlinks, invalid member/package,
  wrong package/member pairing, missing root lock and malformed requests refuse.
- Cyclic path closure terminates validation; Cargo still owns semantic rejection.
- Non-default target-dir configuration still publishes from the pinned tree.

* Rust consumer interface and verifier scope
The pre-BEAM consumer preserves prepare(tree, source, name, custody) as the
version1 wrapper. prepare_request(tree, request, custody) accepts the same
closed version1/version2 object as the fixed recipe. It validates the request
before launching processes, installs and verifies the source-retention root,
then realizes the native product remotely and verifies its final retention.
Version2 snapshot arguments include explicit version/member/package.

Verification independently compares version/source/crate/ABI/target and,
for version2, exact member/package. cargoLibrary must be a bounded Rust
identifier, compiled must name a top-level store object, and the regular
compiled/lib/<cargoLibrary>.so must have the same SHA256 as the regular final
lib/<crate>.so. The fixed Nix recipe parses Cargo.toml and owns actual Cargo
package/library selection. The Rust verifier intentionally adds no partial TOML
parser or verification subprocess; its checks establish identity/byte
consistency, not language execution authority or independent compile causality.

Additional main-thread Rust cases:
- Closed version1 and version2 requests accept; missing/unknown fields, invalid
  versions, malformed/bounded member/package/crate/ABI/source fields refuse.
- A real Source-produced version2 receipt passes Rust verification and
  prepare_request selects the same product bytes with a retained source root.
- A changed member/package/version refuses even when library bytes are intact.
- Changed cargoLibrary naming a missing/different compiled library refuses.
- A non-store compiled address, compiled symlink, or cross-object compiled
  pointer with different library bytes refuses before publication.
- Existing standalone prepare and Source/Rust cross-consumer controls remain.
- Native workspace validator edits change stamp_inputs and invalidate reuse.
